exactGap: Only ZDR is org-pinned today: org-core's RetentionPosture feeds an auth-core claim that Quarry's Claims::zdr_floor raises over request flags, and that floor applies to user tokens only (service tokens are ignored by design). No org or request web policy exists: the edge hard-wires RunPolicy::default() (routes.rs:461, main.rs:1493), two unrelated RunPolicy types exist, control's presets (fast = RobotsIgnore) are never consumed by the edge, and quarry-control's /v1/blocklists entries have no org column and are not read by the edge. The Model Plane gate is one coarse capability (browser.observe/act and browser_agent all map to cap.browser.open) plus capability-core org-scope grants, with no action-class, robots, proxy-tier or header-stripping gates.
reuse: org-core RetentionPosture read endpoint plus auth-core claim stamping as the delivery pattern for a read-only policy posture (org-core types.go:255-315, quarry-edge auth.rs:56-140)
Claims::effective_zdr / zdr_floor as the 'can only raise, never lower' merge semantics to copy for every other gate
BrowserBroker grants: broker-owned allowed_domains (agent_routes.rs validate_run_grant) and the sensitive-action allowlist (grant.go:30-36) as the carrier for action classes
capability-core tenant-bound org-scope grants (engine.go denyOnGrant) and execution-core capability_policy Allow/Deny/Ask
quarry-runtime RunPolicy / DiscoveryPolicy (robots, proxy, block) as the base for one ResolvedPolicy type
BrowserEgressPolicy deny-all default and the existing ZDR refusals (zdr_persistent_profile_forbidden, refuse_durable_job_under_zdr)
constraints: Control Plane owns the org policy of record, Model Plane issues grants, Quarry (Ingestion) enforces or rejects with typed errors; there is no cross-plane DB access, so policy must travel as a signed claim or a grant field. CONFLICT: the claim channel that carries the ZDR floor only reaches user-token callers (gateway UI paths). execution-core and model-gateway call Quarry with service tokens whose zdr claim is true for every org and is deliberately ignored, so for Model-Plane-driven runs the resolved policy has to ride in the BrowserBroker grant or the start-run body set by the Model Plane. Space access must never widen the org policy, the Model can only propose and Quarry executes or rejects, and existing stricter ZDR refusals must not be loosened.
approachAdjustment: Run the ADR first: org-core claims versus capability-core grants (capability-core already has tenant-bound org-scope grants and a single coarse browser capability). Do not describe the ZDR claim as covering the agent path; deliver policy by claim to user-token callers and by grant fields to Model-Plane-driven runs. Ship a Quarry-only thin slice before any org-core storage or admin UI: one ResolvedPolicy replacing the RunPolicy::default() sites, tighten-only merge with the existing zdr floor, typed denials for Evaluate/upload/download (ties to F-t2-002). Reconcile or delete the second RunPolicy type and the unused fast/stealth presets, and wire or retire /v1/blocklists, instead of adding a third policy shape.
effortNote: Kept at L because it spans four planes plus an ADR; treat the Quarry-only slice as M and the org-core/auth-core/broker plumbing as the remaining L.
verdictReason: Direction is right and nothing substantial exists, but the delivery channel is wrong for the agent path, capability-core grants already exist as a competing policy of record, and a Quarry-only first slice is missing from the plan.

exactGap: A right-docked, collapsible chat split already exists (ChatPage.tsx:962-984 mounts ChatLiveRunPanel) and it already reuses BrowserChrome in compact mode (ChatLiveRunPanel.tsx:608) with pause/resume of the AI run (ChatLiveRunPanel.tsx:451), but only for planned and deep-research turns, read-only, and fed by per-step artifact screenshots: browserSessionFromChatRun leaves every live-frame URL null and sessionId undefined so all manual controls stay disabled (chat-run-watch.ts:402-452). The interactive BrowserChrome with takeover, approvals and frame streaming is mounted only in the dashboard Crawl composer (KnowledgeScrapePreview.tsx:253), and there is no dock position, floating composer or new-chat-or-keep rule (only a collapsed flag, chat-run-watch.ts:45).
reuse: ChatLiveRunPanel and its compact BrowserChrome mount (already the docked chat panel)
chat-run-watch.ts adapter (browserSessionFromChatRun) as the view-model seam
gateway browser routes for frames (frame, frames/stream, frames/ws), control (human takeover), timeline and owner-gated artifacts (browser.rs:371-444)
owned_orchestration_run ownership proof for execution-core-owned runs (browser.rs:3347)
ChatWorkspaceCanvas / workCanvasActive layout in ChatPage as the dock host
existing approval refresh and run pause/resume controls in ChatLiveRunPanel
constraints: Frontend Plane owns presentation only; page context may reach the Model Plane only through governed browser.observe results or attachments, never raw DOM from the SPA. A chat turn's browser runs inside execution-core with its own Quarry lease and BrowserBroker grant and is not a gateway browser session (browser.rs:3320-3345), while the dashboard's start_ai_run acquires a separate fresh lease and only re-navigates to the tab's URL (browser.rs:1237,1311-1318), so the user's page and the agent's page are different pages today. User takeover must go through the gateway control route and Quarry control_mode (Model proposes, Quarry executes), and ZDR chat runs have no frames, so dock state must not be persisted server-side and the panel must keep its honest ZDR copy. UI-driven runs still use an interim 'session:{id}' grant_id because real BrowserBroker grant issuance is unbuilt (browser.rs:1235,1258-1262).
approachAdjustment: Split the item. (a) M frontend slice over the existing read-only compact panel: dock positions (right, bottom, maximised, hidden) persisted per user, floating composer, new-chat-or-keep rule. (b) L backend slice for a live, steerable browser in chat: either a gateway projection of execution-core-owned Quarry runs (owner-gated, exposing Quarry's existing frames/ws and control routes) or a chat turn that acts on a user-created session, plus real BrowserBroker grant issuance for UI-driven runs. 'Promote BrowserChrome from the Crawl composer' is also not a fresh extraction: the component is already shared and the chat uses its compact variant.
effortNote: M only covers the dock layout over the existing read-only panel; binding to a live, steerable chat-run session needs gateway, Model Plane and grant work, so the whole item is L.
verdictReason: The docked chat split and the compact BrowserChrome reuse already ship; the real remaining work is dock modes plus a live/takeover session binding that the item underestimates.

exactGap: Phase 1 is fully open: gateway search_web builds its cache key from query, limit, include_answer and filters only (search.rs:209-226), stores with no ZDR check (search.rs:285), keeps entries fresh 4 h and for 24 h with a stale fallback (cache.rs:20-25), and search.rs contains no zdr reference. This is a confirmed cross-tenant path, not only a ZDR gap: the Quarry /v1/search it fronts uses org-scoped private-corpus providers (TantivyLocalIndex, org_id taken from the JWT, search_routes.rs:503-517, local_index.rs module docs) and include_answer feeds an org-scoped answer pipeline, while the gateway key carries no org. Quarry itself is correct (org-keyed SearchCache with no cache read or write under ZDR, search_routes.rs:762-780), a ZDR-aware CacheAdmission already exists privately for the scrape preview (knowledge/quarry.rs:213-280, though its key at line 104 is still target-only), and per-endpoint ZDR refusals exist (routes.rs:563-588); there is no declared per-feature ZDR matrix and no ZDR run tombstone.
reuse: CacheAdmission in knowledge/quarry.rs (promote to a shared gateway module instead of writing a second one)
crate::zdr::{request_zdr, org_zdr_enabled}; org_zdr_enabled already fails closed (assumes ZDR on lookup failure)
authorized_org_id for the cache-key org segment
Quarry's SearchCache::key(org_id, ...) and the ZDR-skips-cache branch in search_routes.rs as the reference admission shape
refuse_durable_job_under_zdr and zdr_persistent_profile_forbidden as the existing refusal-code style for the matrix
quarry-control janitor loop (artifacts only, default off) as the base for a ZDR tombstone sweeper
constraints: Two architecture rules are broken today (ZDR must propagate; no tenant may read another tenant's data), and the gateway is the one boundary the ownership matrix says must hold neither. Frontend Plane gateway owns the fix for phase 1; Quarry (Ingestion) owns the ZDR matrix and any tombstone, and a tombstone must be metadata-only and reviewed against the ZDR contract. Fail closed on ZDR lookup failure as zdr.rs already does. Do not weaken Verevon's stricter existing ZDR refusals when aligning with Firecrawl.
approachAdjustment: Keep phase 1 as written but make it one change: move the private CacheAdmission to a shared module, call it in search_web before lookup and before store, add the authorized org id to the key, and also key the scrape-preview cache by org and request variant (formats, headers, actions). Phase 2: generate or test the ZDR matrix from route attributes in quarry-core rather than hand-maintaining JSON, and do the tombstone only after the contract review.
effortNote: Unchanged: phase 1 is S (one gateway file plus a test), phase 2 is M.
verdictReason: Gap confirmed in code and upgraded from inference to source-verified cross-tenant exposure; the approach is already right and phase 1 is the highest-value quick fix in this batch.

exactGap: Quarry's /step path has no gate for AgentAction::Evaluate: sensitive_approval_for_action covers only respond_dialog, upload_ref and download_ref and falls through to Ok(None) at agent_routes.rs:280, the broker's sensitive-action allowlist has no evaluate (grant.go:30-36), and ChromiumoxideDriver::evaluate runs page.evaluate in the main world (chromiumoxide.rs:3003-3017). The Model Plane half is already done: execution-core's browser.act schema (agent.rs:3479-3512) and the planner ACTION_SCHEMA (llm_planner.rs:53-65) never offer evaluate and the gateway sanitize_action denies it (browser.rs:3751), so exposure is direct service callers of /step plus Quarry's own unwired ModelPlanePlanner prompt, which advertises evaluate and pdf (mp_client.rs:383). The /step path also discards the script's return value (observation.rs:542-543), so a read-only isolated-world evaluate has no consumer there; ActionRuntime::Evaluate (action_runtime.rs:380-392) has no production caller.
reuse: sensitive_approval_for_action + validate_sensitive_approval + the used_sensitive_approval_grants one-shot set (agent_routes.rs:144-310, 2276-2290)
GrantValidation::authorizes_exact_sensitive_action single-action approval rule (grant_validator.rs:98-109)
BrowserBroker allowedSensitiveActions and scoped approval grants (grant.go:30-36)
gateway sanitize_action's typed browser_action_denied response as the denial shape (browser.rs:3751)
require_ephemeral_evidence_action, which already excludes Evaluate in the ephemeral tier (agent_routes.rs:1153-1176)
constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects: the gate must live in quarry-edge/quarry-runtime, not only in the planner schema, and denials must be typed Quarry errors. Grant authority belongs to the Model Plane BrowserBroker (Go), so a new sensitive action class needs a broker allowlist and proto alignment change as well as the Quarry change; approvals are strict single-action one-shot grants and sensitive actions require a parent run grant (agent_routes.rs fails with Forbidden without one). UI-driven runs use an interim 'session:{id}' grant_id today (browser.rs:1235), so the gate must fail closed when no real parent grant exists. Practical severity is defense-in-depth (internal service callers only), not an open user-facing hole.
approachAdjustment: Reduce to a default-deny gate on /step: add 'evaluate' to the broker's allowedSensitiveActions and to sensitive_approval_for_action (bind the script hash into the approval), or simply reject AgentAction::Evaluate on agent runs until a real consumer exists. Drop the 'hide it from the planner unless the grant allows it' sub-task (already true on the Model Plane side) and remove evaluate/pdf from the unwired mp_client planner prompt. Build the isolated-world read-only evaluator (Page.createIsolatedWorld, JSON-only args, size/time/result caps) only together with F-t2-023, because scrape-time actions are where a return value is consumed.
effortNote: S holds for the deny-by-default plus sensitive-approval gate; the isolated-world read-only evaluator is a separate M and should move under F-t2-023.
verdictReason: The Quarry-side gap is real and cheap to close, but half the approach is already shipped on the Model Plane and the read-only-evaluate design is mis-scoped to a path that discards results.

exactGap: No reaper exists: start_run computes ttl_s from max_runtime_s (agent_routes.rs:1446,1502) but nothing reads it, enforce_step_budget checks max_steps only (agent_routes.rs:446-451), and runs leave the in-process registry only through close_run (agent_routes.rs:3623-3626); the 15-minute BrowserBroker grant TTL (server.go:22) bounds use of an abandoned run but not the leaked Chromium pages. There is also no cap on agent runs at all: the agent ChromiumoxideDriver is one shared browser whose acquire never blocks (chromiumoxide.rs:1914-1942, main.rs:1284-1288), and the RuntimeLeasePool(2)/(4) at main.rs:323,337 only gates scrape-render fetches through BrowserDriverAdapter (browser_driver.rs:133-142). The fleet console is routed at /agents/fleets/:fleetId (App.tsx:216) but fetches /v1/fleets directly, the gateway has no /v1/fleets route, its Pause button PATCHes a route the edge does not register (fleet_routes.rs:216-222), and member tiles are placeholder text (FleetRunConsole.tsx:120-130,155-163).
reuse: the run registry and close_run release/receipt/checkpoint path (agent_routes.rs:3600-3650) as the single close routine the sweeper must call
AgentRunCheckpoint, checkpoint_for_entry and the resume_checkpoint flow for non-ZDR resume (agent_routes.rs:453-471, 1425-1445)
Quarry-v2 janitor and the sandbox-manager process Sweeper as sweeper patterns (sandbox-manager is Go in the Model Plane, so copy the pattern, do not import)
existing control_mode (agent_control / human_takeover) as the takeover signal for last_activity
FleetRegistry and fleet_router already in the edge (fleet_routes.rs:216-222) for the console backend
constraints: Ingestion Plane owns the browser lifecycle; Model Plane owns grants, so revocation is a BrowserBroker call and not Quarry's to make (the 15-minute grant TTL already bounds exposure, making explicit revocation optional). A RunEntry owns a process-local Chromium session, so the live registry cannot be shared across edge instances: durable state only enables resume through the existing checkpoint path, and cross-instance steps need sticky routing by run id. ZDR runs are never checkpointed and must stay in memory and simply expire. Reaping must not close a run a user is watching or has taken over.
approachAdjustment: Keep the sweeper and add org-scoped and global run caps at start_run with a typed 429 plus retry-after; cap accounting must also cover UI-created browser sessions, since the SPA has no beforeunload or sendBeacon close so a closed tab or crash leaves the session open. Replace 'move the in-process run registry to durable state for multi-instance operation' with 'checkpoint for resume and use run-id affinity routing'. Treat grant revocation as optional. Fix the fleet console as its own S: gateway proxy for /v1/fleets plus a PATCH/cancel route in the edge, or hide the route until then.
effortNote: Unchanged for sweeper plus caps; the fleet console proxy plus cancel route is a separate S.
verdictReason: The leak and missing caps are real and confirmed; the multi-instance registry idea does not fit a process-local browser, the 2-slot pool evidence applies to scrape rendering, and the grant TTL already narrows the security half.

exactGap: Ref-targeted click, type and select run as in-page DOM operations through Runtime.callFunctionOn: execute_native_target_action checks only isConnected, then calls element.click() or sets the value and dispatches synthetic events (chromiumoxide.rs:1232-1330), and the non-native verified-target path does the same in a page script (chromiumoxide.rs:2026-2093). There is no scroll-into-view, visibility, enabled, stability or covered-element check and no hit-test on the ref path; only click_point (chromiumoxide.rs:2841) dispatches trusted Input.dispatchMouseEvent, the legacy selector click and type use chromiumoxide's scrolling, trusted-event helpers (2828-2915), Press carries only a key string (contracts.rs:699), and the only typed target error is TargetRepairRequired (error.rs:30).
reuse: execute_native_target_action backend-node resolution and per-frame execution-context lookup (chromiumoxide.rs:1232-1290)
click_point's moved/pressed/released Input.dispatchMouseEvent sequence as the trusted dispatch primitive (chromiumoxide.rs:2841-2896)
BrowserDriverCapabilities flag pattern (lib.rs:269-286) to gate the new pipeline per driver
ActionOutcome::unknown(postcondition_required) in observation.rs, which keeps Quarry from claiming a business effect
constraints: Ingestion Plane quarry-browser only; Quarry owns execution and must keep returning an unverified postcondition rather than claim success. The Model Plane browser.act wire schema is a closed list, so new inputs (modifiers, drag, paste) are not reachable by the model without a separate Model Plane contract change. Upload and download reuse the same native click helper and stay approval-gated, so changing the click semantics must not weaken or alter those gates.
approachAdjustment: Direction is right. Express the new failures as ErrorCode::TargetRepairRequired (409) with details.reason (covered_by, not_visible, disabled, unstable) instead of new ErrorCode variants, since ErrorCode is a wire contract shared with the Go, TypeScript and Model Plane clients. Put the pipeline behind a new BrowserDriverCapabilities flag so Browserbase, Browserless and Kernel adapters are unaffected, and leave the synthetic path for governed download clicks until trusted-click download behaviour is verified. Sequence same-frame actionability and trusted dispatch first; the cross-process iframe hit-test and the rich-input phase (modifiers, drag, select_text, paste, virtual clipboard) are separate follow-ups.
effortNote: M holds for same-frame actionability, hit-test, trusted dispatch and typed errors; the OOPIF coordinate transforms and the rich-input phase together are L and should be split out.
verdictReason: Accurately describes a real gap on every AI ref click and type; only the error-contract and capability-flag details need adjusting.

exactGap: Only change_monitor schedules run: workflowFor maps nothing else (schedule_wire.go:39-51), the orchestrator skips workflowless schedules (schedules.go:158-163), and MountScheduleAliases receives a nil Temporal client so trigger and backfill return 501 (control main.go:177-192), although CrawlJobWF, BatchJobWF and ScrapeJobWF are already registered (orchestrator main.go:94-116) and Manager.Trigger/Backfill already exist unused (schedules.go:365-398). The gap is larger than 'skipped': the edge's non-preset create path forwards the raw request (schedule_routes.rs:307-338), whose kind/config/overlap_policy/name keys do not exist on store.Schedule (store.go:333-355), whose Validate requires org_id and target_ref (schedule_validate.go:39-55) while the create handler never reads the org query parameter (resources.go:113-130), so a UI-created scrape, crawl or batch schedule is most likely rejected with 400 at control (INF from reading the code, not executed). Nothing persists config (urls, max_pages, schema), overlap policy, timezone or skipped reasons, and create/update set only CronExpressions (schedules.go:302-327).
reuse: CrawlJobWF, BatchJobWF, ScrapeJobWF (registered) and the ChangeMonitorWF replay-safe run_id derivation from workflow.GetInfo (workflows.go:296-320)
Manager.Trigger and Manager.Backfill in the orchestrator (schedules.go:365-398), already implemented with SKIP/ALLOW_ALL overlap
the orchestrator reconcile loop (30 s pull from control, org-scoped reaper) as the single writer of Temporal schedules
Temporal ScheduleSpec native overlap, jitter and TimeZone instead of a custom Firecrawl-style scheduler
the preset create path in schedule_routes.rs (org and created_by stamped from the verified claim) as the pattern for the other kinds
constraints: Ingestion Plane owns schedules end to end (control, orchestrator, edge); the Frontend gateway should only stop offering overlap, trigger and backfill controls the backend cannot honour. Failure notices go through Application Plane notification-core via its API and entitlement re-checks at fire time must call the Control Plane, with no cross-plane DB reads. ZDR: durable jobs are refused under ZDR (routes.rs:563-588) and the workflow inputs carry no zdr field, so schedule creation must be refused for ZDR orgs and the posture re-checked at fire time. Existing rows must not all start firing at once after the fix, so require an explicit enable step.
approachAdjustment: Add the persistence step first: extend store.Schedule and the control schema with name, config (url/urls, max_pages, schema), overlap policy and timezone, map kind -> target_kind and config -> target_ref/args in the edge, and stamp or require the org from the signed query in the control create handler (the preset path already stamps it). Then extend workflowFor for the three workflows and derive the run_id from the workflow execution exactly as ChangeMonitorWF does; set overlap policy and TimeZone in schedules.go create/update. For trigger and backfill prefer reusing the orchestrator's existing Manager.Trigger/Backfill, reached through a pull-model request row or an internal orchestrator endpoint, over a second Temporal client in quarry-control; the repo's control-side interface (temporal/client.go) was designed for an SDK client there, so record the choice in the ADR.
effortNote: M understated it: store schema and migration, edge-to-control mapping, run_id derivation for three workflows, trigger/backfill plumbing, ZDR and entitlement gating, and an explicit enable step are all required.
verdictReason: The gap is real and already on Quarry's roadmap, but the item misdescribes the failure (creation likely fails rather than silently not firing) and omits the persistence layer that the workflow mapping depends on; effort and approach need adjusting.

exactGap: Scrape cannot run actions or return a screenshot or PDF: ScrapeRequest has only render.waitFor* hints (routes.rs:346-373), the pipeline hard-codes screenshot: None and pdf: None (pipeline.rs:702-703), and signals.actions/screenshot/pdf are planning hints only (driver_plan.rs:13-20). The pieces exist on the agent path only: screenshot via capture_beyond_viewport and PDF via PrintToPdfParams::default() (chromiumoxide.rs:2392-2445), plus ActionRuntime, which has no production caller beyond a lib.rs re-export and acquires its own session rather than using the scrape session in BrowserDriverAdapter::do_fetch (browser_driver.rs:128-240). OSS_PARITY_BACKLOG.md:21-23 marks both as full parity, which is overstated.
reuse: BrowserDriverAdapter::do_fetch, which already sequences acquire, egress policy, goto, wait_for and content on one session (browser_driver.rs:128-240)

the Action enum and ActionScript with on_error (actions.rs:1-80; it already includes Navigate and Evaluate, so both need explicit policy) and the ActionRuntime executor (action_runtime.rs), extended to accept an existing session
driver.screenshot and driver.pdf plus the put_artifact_if_allowed ZDR no-store helper used on the agent path (observation.rs:525-545)
OutputFormats.screenshot/pdf FormatRef fields, which already exist unpopulated (output.rs:140-147)
the tenant-bound artifact read (resource_routes.rs:157) and the gateway owner-gated artifact route for the UI
constraints: Ingestion Plane owns this; the Model proposes scrape actions and Quarry validates, caps and executes them, and selectors or scripts from model output are untrusted input. ZDR: screenshots and PDFs must not be persisted under ZDR (inline-only within a size cap) and the visual page-image producer already writes PNGs only when ZDR is off. Artifacts must be stored under the claim's org. Scrape-time actions must keep the host-pinned browser egress policy that do_fetch derives from the request URL (off-host navigation denied), and Evaluate stays denied until the F-t2-002 gate exists. Cache admission must exclude requests with actions, headers or screenshot options (F-t2-003).
approachAdjustment: Split into two deliverables. (1) Formats (M): capture screenshot and PDF inside do_fetch after goto/wait_for, return the bytes through the fetch response so the pipeline fills OutputFormats.screenshot/pdf as artifacts, with ZDR no-store and cache bypass, and options clip, quality, viewport and fullPage; add tile-and-stitch only past the single-capture height limit. The vision sidecar's tiles (vision.rs, ArtifactKind::Tiles) are OCR/visual-RAG preprocessing, not capture, so do not reuse them. (2) Actions (M): carry a validated, capped Vec<Action> on RenderHints/FetchHints and run it in do_fetch on the same page (extend ActionRuntime to take an existing session instead of acquiring one), returning per-action outputs. Do not run actions through a second ActionRuntime page, because that loses the scrape session's egress and cookie context.
effortNote: Two features (formats and actions), new channels through FetchResponse and the pipeline, cache admission, ZDR handling, API contract and UI; each half alone is M.
verdictReason: Gap confirmed, but the stated integration point (run through the existing ActionRuntime) is not wired to any production path and uses a different session; the item should be split and its hook moved to BrowserDriverAdapter::do_fetch.
